content: The document you provided is a detailed reference list and summary of various guidelines, studies, and resources related to pandemic influenza risk management, preparedness, and response. 1. A review of pandemic influenza preparedness and response strategies was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2007, emphasizing ethical considerations in public health responses to pandemic influenza. This document was accessed in February 2013. 2. The WHO developed a toolkit in 2012 called Communication for Behavioral Impact (COMBI) to guide behavioral and social communication during outbreak responses. This resource was accessed in February 2013. 3. In 2010, the WHO published a document on capacity-building activities during pandemic influenza, which was accessed in April 2013. 4. The WHO released guidelines in 2009 on infection prevention and control during healthcare for confirmed, probable, or suspected cases of pandemic (H1N1) 2009 virus infection and influenza-like illnesses. This document was accessed in February 2013. 5. A 2012 WHO publication provided guidance on the development and implementation of national deployment and vaccination plans for pandemic influenza vaccines. This document was accessed in April 2013. 6. The WHO published a framework in 2009 for behavioral interventions aimed at reducing the transmission and impact of the influenza A (H1N1) virus. This framework was accessed in February 2013. 7. A 2008 WHO guide on outbreak communication planning was accessed in February 2013. 8. The WHO released a rapid risk assessment tool in 2012 for acute public health events, which was accessed in February 2013. 9. A 2009 WHO document discussed the use of rapid diagnostic tests for influenza, which was accessed in February 2013. 10. The WHO Regional Office for Europe published a toolkit in 2012 for assessing health system capacity for crisis management. This document was accessed in February 2013. 11. A joint statement by the Global Health Workforce Alliance, WHO, IFRC, UNICEF, and UNHCR in 2011 emphasized scaling up the community-based health workforce for emergencies. This statement was accessed in February 2013. 12. The WHO published a training package in 2011 for community health workers on managing cases during an influenza outbreak. This resource was accessed in February 2013. 13. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control published a review of pandemics in the 20th and 21st centuries, which was accessed in April 2013. 14. A study by Vynnycky, Trindall, and Mangtani in 2007 estimated the reproduction numbers of the Spanish influenza using morbidity data, published in the International Journal of Epidemiology. 15. Jackson, Vynnycky, and Mangtani published a 2010 study in the American Journal of Epidemiology estimating the transmissibility of the 1918 influenza pandemic, with evidence of increased transmissibility between successive waves. 16. Miller et al. (2009) discussed the signature features of influenza pandemics and their implications for policy in the New England Journal of Medicine. 17. Taubenberger and Morens (2006) described the 1918 influenza as the mother of all pandemics in Emerging Infectious Diseases. 18. Fraser et al. (2009) analyzed the pandemic potential of a strain of Influenza A (H1N1) in Science. 19. Van Kerkhove et al. (2013) conducted a meta-analysis of serological studies from 19 countries to estimate age-specific cumulative incidence during the 2009 influenza pandemic, published in Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses. 20. Dawood et al. (2012) estimated global mortality associated with the first 12 months of the 2009 H1N1 pandemic in a modeling study published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 21. The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) published a 2009 document on risk management and risk assessment techniques (ISO/IEC 31010:2009). 22. Ejima et al. (2012) explored the time required to estimate the case fatality ratio of influenza using joint estimation of virulence and transmission potential, published in Computational and Mathematical Methods in Medicine. 23. Garske et al. (2009) assessed the severity of the novel influenza A/H1N1 pandemic in the British Medical Journal. 24. Van Kerkhove et al. (2011) identified risk factors for severe outcomes following 2009 influenza A (H1N1) infection in a global pooled analysis published in PLoS Medicine. 25. A 2010 review by the Public Health Agency of Canada and Health Canada evaluated lessons learned from the 2009 H1N1 pandemic response. 26. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia published a guide in 2006 for conducting tabletop exercises for national influenza pandemic preparedness. 27. The WHO released a manual in 2011 for the laboratory diagnosis and virological surveillance of influenza. 28. Recommendations and laboratory procedures for detecting avian influenza A (H5N1) virus in specimens from suspected human cases were published by the WHO in 2007. 29. The WHO published emergency guidelines in 2010 for managing adult patients with complications of pandemic influenza A (H1N1) 2009 in limited-resource settings. 30. The WHO released guidelines in 2009 for pandemic preparedness and response in the non-health sector, emphasizing a whole-of-society approach. 31. Recommendations for good practices in pandemic preparedness, based on evaluations of the 2009 H1N1 response, were published by the WHO Regional Office for Europe in 2010. 32. Longini et al. (2005) discussed strategies for containing pandemic influenza at the source in Science. 33. Ferguson et al. (2006) proposed strategies for mitigating an influenza pandemic in Nature. 34. The WHO guidance document on pandemic influenza risk management was revised in 2013, incorporating feedback from technical experts and external peer reviewers. 35. Planning for future influenza pandemics requires assumptions about epidemiology to guide public health decision-making and resource allocation. These assumptions are based on data from seasonal influenza, avian influenza, and past pandemics but are not predictive of future pandemics. 36. Modes of transmission for pandemic influenza are expected to be similar to seasonal influenza, primarily through large droplets or contact, with potential contributions from airborne particles. Preventive measures include good hand hygiene, isolation of ill individuals, and the use of personal protective equipment during aerosol-generating procedures.
